topic: Integrated evaluation of evidence completeness and omission for temporally evolving multi-source free-form generation, with calibrated selective prediction under non-stationary distribution shift

gaps.description: No admitted study validates one end-to-end evaluation scheme that jointly measures claim correctness, evidence attribution correctness, citation or evidence completeness, temporal or current-state correctness, omission, calibrated uncertainty, and abstention while preserving separate denominators for those dimensions. The corpus validates individual components and smaller combinations.
gaps.suggested_search_query: "joint evaluation framework" factuality attribution completeness temporal correctness omission calibration abstention "free-form generation" multi-source
gaps.resolution_notes: Still open after round 3. Papers 2405.00982, 2604.03141, 2606.29054, 2607.19322, and doi-10-1109-access-2026-3679691 strengthen omission-sensitive recall, citation verification, temporal evidence validity, selective generation, and risk control, but the synthesis finds no admitted study validating all required dimensions jointly while retaining dimension-specific denominators.

gaps.description: The corpus contains no direct evaluation on private workplace email or Teams-style communication with realistic revisions, quoted history, conflicting updates, delayed or out-of-order arrival, versioned attachments, and permission-constrained evidence. Target-domain fixtures and gold data remain an engineering validation gap.
gaps.resolution_notes: Resolve by constructing a permission-safe target-domain benchmark or synthetic/replayed fixture suite covering threaded email and chat, quoted history, conflicting and superseding updates, delayed and out-of-order events, attachment revisions, evidence visibility constraints, and explicit gold work-item states. Define gold claims, source/version provenance, temporal validity intervals, omissions, and expected abstentions, then run the evaluation stack on these fixtures. Existing adjacent-domain papers can inform scenario design but cannot substitute for target-domain validation.

gaps.description: The corpus does not establish a general evidence-completeness method that jointly handles compound claims, partially supportive evidence, multiple complementary sources, and temporally versioned evidence. Separate studies cover subsets of these conditions.
gaps.suggested_search_query: "evidence completeness" compound claims partial support complementary evidence multi-source temporal versioning provenance evaluation
gaps.resolution_notes: Still open after round 3. Papers 2404.15588, 2508.20867, doi-10-18653-v1-2025-acl-long-837, and doi-10-1109-access-2026-3679691 cover minimal evidence groups, partial-support attribution, multi-source aggregation, or temporal validity, but the synthesis finds no admitted method jointly treating all four as one general evidence-completeness problem.

gaps.description: Report-level omission has substantial benchmark coverage, but the corpus still does not establish omission detection for evolving workplace work items, due information, superseded facts, or decision-relevant state across time.
gaps.suggested_search_query: "omission detection" longitudinal summarization work-item state superseded facts due dates temporal updates decision-relevant information
gaps.resolution_notes: Still open after round 3. Papers 2405.00982, 2512.17776, 2604.03141, 2607.19322, 2410.14964, manual-39435af3dd, and doi-10-6028-nist-sp-500-321-realtime-overview strengthen omission, novelty, update-summarization, and temporal evaluation, but none is reported by the synthesis as evaluating omission of evolving workplace work-item state, due information, and supersession over time.

gaps.description: A target-domain human-review protocol remains an engineering gap: representative or risk-stratified sampling, minimum human-review volume, multi-rater adjudication, confusion matrices, abstention treatment, coverage reporting, and validation of any LLM-assisted judge against independent human judgments remain project-specific choices.
gaps.resolution_notes: Resolve by specifying and piloting a project-level annotation and audit protocol: define representative and risk-stratified sampling strata; determine review volume using precision or power targets; establish rater training, blinded independent labeling, adjudication rules, and disagreement reporting; define confusion matrices and dimension-specific denominators; treat abstentions as a separate outcome with coverage-risk reporting; and validate any LLM-assisted judge on an independently human-labeled holdout before operational use. Papers 2406.07967, 2605.16354, 2606.00093, manual-32d5793dca, doi-10-18653-v1-w19-8642, and manual-f5ce52cae2 can inform the design but do not determine these project-specific parameters.

gaps.description: The corpus demonstrates evaluator-optimization effects, rating indeterminacy, abstention sensitivity, and directional judge bias but does not provide a project-specific procedure for preventing acceptance criteria from being overfit to the same automatic evaluator used during development. Independent holdouts, evaluator separation, and regression checks remain an engineering validation problem.
gaps.resolution_notes: Resolve by separating development and acceptance evaluators, freezing an independent human-reviewed holdout before tuning, prohibiting optimization against final acceptance labels, maintaining multiple heterogeneous evaluators where practical, tracking dimension-specific regressions rather than one aggregate score, periodically re-auditing automatic judges against independent humans, and adding adversarial or evaluator-disagreement cases to regression tests. Evidence from 2212.08037, 2512.17776, 2606.00093, 2607.08700, and manual-32d5793dca motivates these controls but does not prescribe the project's exact isolation protocol.

gaps.description: Calibration under continuing temporal or distributional change remains open for non-stationary free-form communication streams. The corpus supplies adaptive coverage results, cross-domain calibration studies, benchmark-aging evidence, and structured-generation risk-control results, but not one validated selective-prediction method for continuously changing workplace communication.
gaps.suggested_search_query: "selective prediction" "non-stationary" free-form generation online calibration concept drift abstention adaptive conformal temporal stream
gaps.resolution_notes: Still open after round 3. Papers 2106.00170, 2302.07869, 2404.00474, 2505.23912, 2510.07238, 2602.16537, and 2606.29054 provide evidence on adaptive or strongly adaptive conformal inference, drift-aware calibration, cross-domain linguistic calibration, and structured-generation risk control, but the synthesis finds no validated selective-prediction procedure for continuously changing workplace free-form communication streams.

convergence.next_round_topic: Joint evaluation and selective prediction for temporally evolving multi-source generation: evidence completeness for compound and partially supported claims, longitudinal omission of superseded or due work-item state, and online calibration under non-stationary streams
